adversarial_review.check: The cross block uses c_ij/sqrt(pi_i*pi_j) and the two directed rates use the same conductance normalization.
The edgewise factorization is applied only to disjoint nonempty core and tail supports.
Negative, nonfinite and out-of-range capacity inputs are rejected before taking a square root.
The exact restricted cross norm is required to lie below sqrt(rho_C*rho_T); an excess is rejected.
All nonpositive Q3 capacity reserves are retained and never clipped to zero.
The two block-mean modes and their Schur complement are not included in this residual capacity estimate.
Finite capacity diagnostics do not establish uniformity, a GNS gap, a continuum limit or a physical mass gap.

boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite edgewise capacity envelope only. The all-nonpositive Q3 capacity reserves are a sufficient-budget boundary, not a physical gaplessness theorem.
decision_reason: The weighted edgewise Cauchy envelope is exact at the finite algebraic level and dominates every tested R-422 cross norm, but its capacity reserve is nonpositive on all 114 eligible Q3 rows. The estimate therefore identifies a route boundary rather than a uniform coercivity result.
decision_scope: Finite directed boundary-capacity envelope on the fixed R-422 Q3 grid; no tier change.
finding: The primary lane passes 2209/2209 assertions over 858 conditional rows and 114 eligible residual rows. The exact R-422 cross norm is below sqrt(rho_C*rho_T) on every eligible row. Capacities range from 2.5432351046609147 to 3654.481957885938 and capacity reserves range from -3650.2671476576393 to -1.7429838727911164, so all 114 eligible Q3 rows are nonpositive under this sufficient envelope. The non-importing lane passes 40/40 on four fixtures with three positive and one nonpositive reserves, hostile passes 7/7, integrated passes 18/18 and Lean R423 compiles.

formal_integration.lean: R423 PASS; scalar capacity envelope only

method: Reuse the hash-pinned R-419 law, conductance, R-421 tail floor and R-422 residual split without retuning.
Define the directed core and tail boundary rates and factor the transformed cross edge into two nonnegative Cauchy factors.
Evaluate the capacity reserve min(a,kappa)-sqrt(rho_C*rho_T) and compare it with the exact restricted cross norm on every eligible row.
Reconstruct the inequality on non-importing reversible fixtures, reject invalid inputs and forged reserves, and compile the scalar Lean cross-check.
Retain the all-nonpositive Q3 sufficient-budget boundary without clipping or physical promotion.
next_action: Derive a sharper localized boundary-capacity estimate on a Hamiltonian common core, then combine it with the coarse Schur sector and the R-399/R-415 history transfer.
no_overclaim: The capacity envelope is a finite sufficient bound. Its nonpositive Q3 reserves do not prove physical gaplessness, and no C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or mass-gap claim follows.
question: Can the R-422 residual cross norm be replaced by an explicit directed boundary-capacity Cauchy envelope, and does the resulting finite reserve remain positive on the fixed Q3 grid?
title: Finite directed boundary-capacity Cauchy envelope
